description:
## Why

PKIX-baac.5 shipped Merkle inclusion proof and STH signature verification (RFC 6962 §2.1.1 / §3.5) with synthetic-but-algorithm-correct fixtures: a Python oracle builds a tiny Merkle tree of 7 leaves, signs a synthetic STH committing to its root, and a separate independent verify-side algorithm (RFC 9162 §2.1.3.2) cross-checks every proof. openssl additionally independently validates the STH signature against the SPKI and signed-input bytes.

The bead's acceptance criterion 2 ('One real-world inclusion proof verifies against a real STH') is met in algorithm-shape but not in literal real-world bytes. A captured live-log triple from e.g. Google Argon2024 or Cloudflare Nimbus 2024 would provide extra defense in depth against any subtle wire-format divergence between pkix-ct's interpretation and what real CT logs emit.

## What

1. Pick a currently-usable RFC 6962 log (Argon2024 or Nimbus 2024 are fine choices).
2. Fetch one cert's SCT (from a CT-enforcing TLS site's cert), its inclusion proof via the log's get-proof-by-hash endpoint, and a contemporary STH via get-sth.
3. Commit the captured triple (cert.der, sct.bin, audit-path.bin, sth.bin, log-spki.der) as offline fixtures under pkix-ct/tests/fixtures/.
4. Add an integration test that wires them together: parse the cert, derive the leaf hash for the precert form, verify the inclusion proof against the STH's root_hash, and verify the STH signature against the log's published SPKI.

## Out of scope

- Live network calls during tests. The capture is one-off; the test runs fully offline.
- Automated capture in CI. If the captured STH ages out, the test will still verify (since pkix-ct doesn't enforce STH freshness), but maintainers may want to refresh periodically.

## Filed as

Follow-up to PKIX-baac.5. Algorithm correctness is established by PKIX-baac.5's synthetic-oracle work; this bead just adds a concrete real-world byte-equality data point.
notes:
Closed 2026-05-11 (do-beads autonomous loop).

Delivered:
- pkix-ct/tests/fixtures/live-log/capture_live_log.py — one-off network-capture script that finds a currently-running CT log from the Google v3 log list, captures a precert SCT from a CT-enforcing TLS site (default: cloudflare.com), computes the RFC 6962 §3.4 MerkleTreeLeaf and its leaf hash, fetches the matching inclusion proof and a contemporary STH, and writes everything as offline fixtures.
- Captured triple from Cloudflare Nimbus2026 (currently-usable log shard) at tree_size=4188754631, leaf_index=4172671010 (audit-path length 30). meta.json records full provenance.
- pkix-ct/tests/live_log.rs — integration test that runs verify_sct_for_precert + verify_sth + verify_inclusion end-to-end against the captured triple. All 3 pkix-ct entry points pass.

Independent oracles cross-validate the fixture:
1. Cloudflare's get-proof-by-hash endpoint accepted the leaf hash my script computed — the log itself confirms the §3.4 byte form is correct.
2. A pure-Python RFC 9162 §2.1.3.2 verifier inside the capture script re-verifies the inclusion proof against the STH root.
3. openssl dgst -verify independently confirms the STH ECDSA-SHA256 signature against the log SPKI.

Follow-up filed: PKIX-yzb6 (ship a public MerkleTreeLeaf builder helper so future capture scripts and CT consumers don't have to re-implement §3.4).
title: pkix-ct: capture a live-log SCT+inclusion+STH triple as offline fixture
